# The Press Release Is Dead. MKBHD Just Proved It.

Samsung didn't need a press conference. They needed one creator with a camera and 18 million subscribers.

When MKBHD posted his Galaxy S26 Ultra coverage — casually calling the privacy display feature "pretty damn cool" — it generated over 33,000 likes and 2,700 retweets. That's not media coverage. That's a product launch. And the distinction matters enormously if you're building anything that needs to reach an audience in 2025.

We've been watching this shift happen in slow motion for years. Now it's complete. Here's what that actually means for builders and operators.

---

**Traditional media validates. Creators convert.**

Tech journalism tells people a product exists. A creator like MKBHD makes people *want* it. Those are fundamentally different jobs — and only one of them drives the engagement numbers Samsung just saw. When you're planning a product launch strategy, the question is no longer "did we get press coverage?" It's "did we get the right creator to genuinely engage with what we built?"

---

**Authenticity is the distribution moat.**

MKBHD's audience trusts him because he has a reputation for calling things as he sees them. "Pretty damn cool" lands differently coming from him than it does in a Samsung press release. That trust took years to build and cannot be bought outright — only earned through genuine product quality and smart relationship-building. The moment creators become pure ad vehicles, the moat disappears. The brands that understand this partner *with* creators, not just *through* them.

---

**This model scales to entertainment, gaming, and beyond.**

The Samsung story is a hardware story on the surface. Underneath it's a distribution blueprint. Film studios, game developers, and entertainment platforms are still over-indexing on traditional PR cycles and under-investing in creator relationships. The gaming space is particularly behind on this. A single authentic post from the right creator at the right moment of a launch cycle can outperform an entire press junket — and cost a fraction of it. The math is obvious. The execution is where most teams fail.

---

**The creator *is* the channel. Build your strategy accordingly.**

Stop thinking about creators as a line item in your marketing budget. Start thinking about them as primary distribution infrastructure. That means building relationships before you need them, giving creators genuine early access, and accepting that authentic coverage requires relinquishing some control over the narrative. That last part is where most operators flinch — and where the real opportunity lives for those who don't.

---

MKBHD didn't cover the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra because Samsung paid him to be excited. He covered it because the privacy display feature was worth covering. That's the entire lesson.

The brands and builders who win the next five years of consumer attention won't be the ones with the biggest ad budgets. They'll be the ones who built products worth talking about and then got them into the right hands at the right time.

Samsung got both right this cycle.

**What's your current creator partnership strategy — and is it built for distribution or just awareness? There's a massive difference between the two.**
source_story_title: Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra 'Privacy Display' Feature Showcased by MKBHD
source_story_summary: Top tech YouTuber Marques Brownlee (@MKBHD) highlighted the Galaxy S26 Ultra's new 'privacy display' feature, calling it 'pretty damn cool,' and released a full video covering additional device details. The post generated substantial engagement with over 33,000 likes and 2,700 retweets, signaling strong consumer interest in the upcoming Samsung flagship.
